project_specification.project_name: nullius — HTTP API transport: every refusal carries the error class
project_specification.addition_summary: Extend the api workspace member (packages/api, import name nullius_api) so that every refusal it answers carries, alongside the code word and the message feature 4 already puts in the envelope, the error class — the greppable class name of the refusal that was raised, spelled by the member that owns it. The transport already answers four refusal statuses through one writing door (nullius_api.server.error_payload): 400 for a malformed ask, 404 for an unknown path, 405 with an Allow header for a wrong verb, and 503 naming the missing configuration for an unconfigured component, a member's typed refusal, or the server's own unexpected fault — plus 501 for a route with no adapter yet and 500 for an unencodable payload. Today the envelope is {"error": {"code": ..., "message": ...}}; this feature widens it to {"error": {"code": ..., "class": ..., "message": ...}} at every one of those doors, so a caller can route on the class the member raised without parsing the message. The class is a name the member owns and would state in a traceback (FdrDeployMetricError, CoverageError, DebitChargeError, ForwardRecordError, PromotionRequestError, ...), so carrying it is not the leak the law forbids — the law forbids a traceback or a filesystem path, and a bare class name is neither. The work is one signature change to the envelope factory and a class argument at each of its call sites, plus the tests that pin that every refusal shape now carries the class and that no body carries a traceback or a filesystem path. No route's status, no message, no success behaviour, and no other member changes.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (members under packages/*, composed by src/app/module_loader.create_app) / SQLite stores addressed by DATABASE_URL / pytest (ruff conventions)
existing_context.test_baseline: workspace suite tests/ passing; member suites under packages/*/tests (api, ops, promotion, forward, providers ...) all passing on main. Measure the real numbers by running the suite before relying on them.
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, frozen dataclasses for value types, stdlib-first members (a member adds no third-party lockfile edge unless it must), docstrings citing app_spec.xml feature numbers and docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md sections, refusals raised as typed errors whose message opens with a greppable code word and names the one repair, degrade-don't-break composition (a builder returns None when its environment is unconfigured), @register only in a package __init__, cross-member imports deferred past module scope. Tests assert observed behaviour with narrative docstrings. Member suites and the workspace suite are run as separate pytest invocations. Feature 4 already built the transport's one writing door: nullius_api.server._write_json writes every body, error_payload(code, message) is the single envelope factory, and the send_error override closes the base class's HTML protocol-error path to the same envelope. Member refusals are recognised by module-path segment and answered 503 with the member's message; unexpected faults answer a generic 500 naming nothing. The envelope never carries a traceback or a filesystem path.

category.name: HTTP API Transport
category.feature: System widens the one error envelope so every refusal returns an error.class field naming the refusal's own class, alongside the code word and the error message.

System returns the refusal's own class at each of the envelope's call sites: the malformed-ask 400, the unknown-route 404, the wrong-verb 405, the unconfigured-component 503, the member-refusal 503 (the raised exception's own class name), the route-not-implemented 501, the generic internal error, the unencodable-payload 500 and the base class's protocol-error door.

System passes an end-to-end sweep asserting every refusal shape answers the widened envelope carrying a non-empty class, that the member-refusal class names the refusal the member raised, and that no body carries a traceback or a filesystem path.

project_specification.integration_points: error_payload gains one keyword, class (defaulting to the bare base so a call site that names no class still answers a class), and every refusal branch in nullius_api.server passes the class it knows: the transport's own refusals pass a stable class name they own (the malformed-ask, unknown- route, wrong-verb, unconfigured, not-implemented and internal-error doors each name their own class), and the member-refusal door passes the raised exception's own class name (type(exc).__name__) — the same class a member's traceback would name, which is why carrying it is not the leak the law forbids. The class is spelled as a plain string in the envelope, never a live object, so the codec and every caller read it the same way they read code and message. No route's status, message, success behaviour, the _write_json door, the send_error override, the route table, the entrypoint, or any other member changes. Covered by packages/api/tests.
project_specification.constraints: - error_payload keeps its two positional arguments (code, message); the class is a third, keyword-only argument with a default, so every existing call site and every existing test keeps working unchanged and the envelope gains a field rather than reshaping. - The class is a name the refusal's own member would state (a bare class name such as FdrDeployMetricError), never a traceback, a filesystem path, a module path, or request-derived text. The member-refusal door carries type(exc).__name__ only; it never echoes str(exc) into the class. - No response body carries a traceback or a filesystem path, including a member refusal whose message quotes a leaked store URL — the class field does not become a second place a path could leak. - No route's HTTP status, message, or success behaviour changes, and no other member, the route table, the entrypoint, src/app/module_loader.py, the root pyproject.toml, pytest.ini, migrations/** or settings changes. - The api member uses only the standard library for HTTP; it adds no third-party dependency to uv.lock. - All existing workspace and member tests must stay green.

implementation_steps.step: Phase 1 — widen the envelope factory. Give error_payload a keyword-only class argument (defaulting to a stable base name such as "Error" so a call site that names no class still answers a class). The envelope becomes {"error": {"code": ..., "class": ..., "message": ...}}. Update the docstring: the class is the refusal's own name, carried so a caller routes on it without parsing the message, and it is never a traceback or a filesystem path.

Phase 2 — carry the class at every door. Each refusal branch in _dispatch_by_table, the belt around it, _write_json's unencodable-payload fallback, and the send_error override passes the class it owns: the malformed ask, the unknown route, the wrong verb, the unconfigured component, the route not implemented, the generic internal error, and the protocol error each name their own stable class; the member-refusal door names type(exc).__name__, the class the served member raised. Keep the member-recognition logic and the 503/500 split exactly as feature 4 left them — only the class field is added.

Phase 3 — the tests. Add a suite in packages/api/tests asserting: every refusal shape (400, 404, 405, 503 unconfigured, 503 member refusal, 501, 500, and the base class's protocol error) answers an envelope that carries a non-empty class; the member-refusal class names the raised exception's own class (e.g. FdrDeployMetricError); the transport's own doors answer their stable class names; no body carries a traceback, a filesystem path, or a ".py" suffix — including a member refusal whose message quotes a leaked store URL; and a call site that omits the class still answers a class (the default). Feature 4's existing tests stay green unchanged (they assert code and message, which are untouched).

Phase 4 — verify. Run the api member's own suite (uv run pytest packages/api/tests) and the repository-level suite (uv run pytest tests/), both, and confirm all pass. Lint only the changed files against a sibling (the repo lint is red on main).

project_specification.success_criteria: Every refusal the api member answers — 400, 404, 405, 503 (unconfigured and member), 501 and 500 — carries a non-empty error class alongside the code word and the message The member-refusal class names the refusal the served member raised, and the transport's own doors answer their own stable class names No response body carries a traceback, a filesystem path, or a module path Feature 4's envelope (code, message) and every route's status and success behaviour are unchanged; all existing workspace and member tests still green
